A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViRC/CRUX research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ViRC training and benchmark evaluations, component ablations, training dynamics, and qualitative reasoning examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds pretrained-model comparisons, teacher evaluation, broader benchmark results, and inference-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The CRU construction, visual tools, four reasoning patterns, three-stage training procedure, and reward design remain unchanged. Additional Qwen2-VL experiments apply the existing pipeline. The 50K SFT subset now mentioned in the main text was already specified in v1 Appendix C.1–C.2.

E1.justification: v3 Table 11 adds actual evaluation on MathVision, We-Math, MathVerse, and LogicVista, substantially expanding the mathematical problem collections and visual logical-reasoning coverage. CRUX training coverage and the original mathematical and high-resolution benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 9–10 newly evaluate Qwen2-VL-2B/7B baselines and Qwen2.5-VL-72B as a teacher comparator; previously the latter served as an annotation/reward model. The main comparator sets remain unchanged. MM-Eureka becoming MM-Eureka-Qwen-7B is a naming clarification.

E3.justification: v3 adds Qwen2-VL-2B/7B experimental configurations and an inference-cost protocol across the benchmarks in Tables 10–11. This measures text/visual tokens and latency, including the longest/slowest 1% of cases, using controlled hardware and inference settings. Existing benchmark and ablation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1 adds substantive analyses of robustness to pretrained-model choice, performance relative to the annotation teacher, and computational efficiency with and without CRUs. These address questions absent from v1, while its component ablations and qualitative cases remain.

E5.justification: Neither version documents repeated-run uncertainty, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new top-1% cost summaries describe instance-level resource usage; they do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores are retained, but Tables 9–12 add substantial results. These include ViRC-Qwen2VL averages of 44.20/64.32, teacher-versus-ViRC averages of 75.12/77.79, a 48.83 average across four additional benchmarks, and ViRC inference costs of 879 tokens and 2.31 seconds on average. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: The CRU definitions, relationships between reasoning paradigms, and GRPO objective and advantage equations are mathematically unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: Reason Chunking, CRUX, and progressive training. The headline 18.8% mathematical improvement and cross-domain generalization claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix E.1 newly interprets results as robustness to pretrained-model and resolution-policy choices, benefits beyond teacher distillation, and efficiency gains from chunking. The existing domain-shift interpretation is condensed rather than removed. No substantial new limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: v3 specifies vLLM v0.14.1, a single A100 80G GPU, batch size 1, and FP16 for cost measurements. It also explicitly identifies the RL source pool as the same 50K subset. Existing training hyperparameters, prompts, tool specifications, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Six references are added for vLLM, Qwen2-VL, and the four additional benchmarks. Appendix E.1 adds contextual justification for comparing against MINT-CoT. The related-work section and the central positioning against static-image and step-wise visual reasoning remain substantively stable.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammatical edits, clarifies training-subset wording, and reorganizes Appendix E.1 into focused paragraphs while shortening its domain-shift discussion. Affiliation wording, acknowledgments, and the supplementary author header are updated; the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Four new appendix tables display backbone, teacher, additional-benchmark, and cost comparisons. Existing detailed ablation tables become Tables 13–16 with formatting adjustments, and Figure 4 and Table 6 are repositioned. The established figures and qualitative/prompt panels are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The added evaluations and controlled inference-cost measurements strengthen empirical support for generality and efficiency. Reporting errors temper this benefit: Table 11 gives MINT-CoT an average of 38.54 although its four entries average 38.05, and Table 8's new three-benchmark averaging description conflicts with its retained six-subset averages. These inconsistencies reduce precision without reversing the added comparisons.
